items.headline: FDA approves first RNA-based therapy for generalized myasthenia gravis
items.summary: The FDA approved cemdisiran, sold as Livsayis, as the first therapy of its kind for adults with generalized myasthenia gravis, a disease where the immune system attacks the connections between nerves and muscles. In a large trial, patients taking the drug improved far more than those on a placebo, and it only needs to be injected four times a year.
items.why_it_matters: It gives patients with this disabling autoimmune disease a new option that needs dosing only a few times a year instead of constant treatment.
